name: glidesort (stable hybrid merge/quick sort)
baseline: slice::sort and sort_unstable as of rustc 1.69 nightly (before driftsort and ipnsort)
verdict_reason: glidesort's published lead was measured against the pre-1.81 std sorts, and its own numbers are a chart image. std's driftsort (1.81) applies the same ideas; the driftsort writeup finds the two close on most patterns, with glidesort ahead only on some partially sorted and low-cardinality inputs, at about 5x driftsort's binary size.
tier_reason: First-party results are only in a chart image; the only text numbers are binary-size figures from the driftsort writeup.
claimed_speedup: Chart only (Apple M1, u64, rustc 1.69.0-nightly). Binary size per u64 instantiation: 25520 bytes for glidesort vs 5294 for driftsort and 2335 for the previous std slice::sort; about 13x the old sort, against about 2.5x for driftsort.
workload: Sorting u64 slices across input distributions (chart); binary size of one instantiation (writeup).
one_liner: Stable sort mixing powersort run merging with stable quicksort; its ideas now ship in std's driftsort, which narrows the gap.
how_it_is_fast: glidesort scans for sorted runs like powersort but defers sorting unsorted stretches, merging logical runs and sorting them with a branchless stable quicksort only when needed. It interleaves several merges for memory- and instruction-level parallelism.
use_it_when: You are pinned to a Rust toolchain older than 1.81 and need a faster stable sort.
You need sorting with a caller-provided buffer (sort_with_buffer) or bounded auxiliary memory.
skip_it_when: On Rust 1.81 or later for general use: std's slice::sort is close on most patterns and much smaller.
Binary size or compile time matters.
caveats: First-party benchmark exists only as a chart image, against std sorts that have since been replaced.
tradeoffs: Large code size per instantiation (25520 bytes for u64 in release) and longer compile times, per the driftsort writeup.

evidence.quote: driftsort is similar in terms of effective capabilities to glidesort while only requiring ~2.5x the binary-size in contrast to ~13x for glidesort.
random_p5 sees the only major difference between driftsort and glidesort at this input length.
